name: Hot Dice
intro: A short path through Hot Dice: which dice score, then why keeping fewer dice can be better and when to bank your points.

units.name: How Hot Dice works
units.blurb: Scoring dice, farkles and hot dice.

lessons.title: Scoring combos
lessons.summary: In Hot Dice, 1s, 5s and three of a kind score, and a few big combos score more. Learn to spot every scoring die in a roll.
lessons.wrap: 1s, 5s, three of a kind, straights and three pairs. Next: a quick rules check.

steps.text:
Roll six dice and set aside at least one scoring die. Then roll the rest to add more, or bank your points. If a roll has no scoring dice, you farkle and lose the turn’s points. First to 4,000 wins.

Each 1 scores 100 and each 5 scores 50.
Find the scoring dice in this roll.
steps.wrong: Only 1s and 5s score on their own.

steps.text: Three of a kind scores the number × 100, so three 4s score 400. Three 1s score 1,000. Four, five or six of a kind double, triple or quadruple that.
steps.wrong: Look for three of the same number.

steps.text: Two big combos only count in a single roll of all six dice: a straight 1–6 scores 1,500 and three pairs score 750.
steps.explain: Three pairs: 750. Score all six dice and it’s hot dice: you roll all six again and keep adding.

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Five questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the strategy.

lessons.title: Hot Dice rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Hot Dice rules: single 1s and 5s, three of a kind, farkles, hot dice and the winning score.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the decisions.

steps.wrong: A 5 scores alone, and so do three of a kind.

steps.prompt: You roll and no die scores. What happens?
options: You keep your points and pass
You lose the points from this turn
steps.explain: That’s a farkle: the turn’s points are lost. Points you’ve banked before are safe.

steps.prompt: Every one of your six dice has scored this turn. What now?
options: You may roll all six again
steps.explain: Hot dice: roll all six again and keep adding to the same turn.

steps.prompt: What score wins the game here?

units.name: Keeping and banking
units.blurb: Which dice to keep and when to stop.

lessons.title: Keep fewer, roll more
lessons.summary: You don’t have to keep every scoring die. In Hot Dice, keeping just a 1 and rolling five dice is often better than keeping a 1 and a 5.
lessons.wrap: More dice means fewer farkles and more big combos. Next: when to bank.

steps.text:
You can keep the 1 and the 5 for 150 and roll four dice, or keep just the 1 for 100 and roll five.

The fewer dice you roll, the more often you farkle: about 8% with five dice, 16% with four, 28% with three, 44% with two and 67% with one.
The extra 50 isn’t worth giving up a die.
steps.prompt: Tap the one die you should keep.
steps.wrong: Keep the bigger single score and roll the rest.
steps.done: Keep the 1 and roll five. Five dice farkle half as often as four.

steps.explain: One 5 keeps five dice in play for just 50 points less.

options: Yes: 1,000 is too good to give back
No: keep one 1 and roll five
steps.explain: Keep the 1,000. The rule is about small extras like a lone 5, not big combos.

lessons.title: When to bank
lessons.summary: Bank too early and you score slowly; roll too long and you farkle. Learn the simple banking rule for Hot Dice and when to break it.
lessons.wrap: Around 350 with three or more dice, anything over 300 with one or two, and push harder when you’re behind. The same thinking helps in Five Dice and Ship, Captain and Crew: count your chances before you roll again.

steps.text: You kept a 1 and rolled five dice.
steps.prompt: Tap the scoring dice in this roll.
steps.wrong: Look for three of a kind.
steps.done: Three 5s add 500. That’s 600 this turn, with two dice left to roll.

steps.text: A simple guide: with three or more dice left, keep rolling until you have about 350 to 400. With one or two dice left, bank anything over 300.
steps.prompt: 600 points, two dice left. Roll or bank?
steps.explain: Bank. Two dice farkle about 44% of the time, so you’d risk 600 for a small gain.

position.label: A new turn: your first roll

steps.text: Early in a turn, you keep the three 2s for 200.
steps.prompt: 200 points, three dice left to roll. Roll or bank?
steps.explain: Roll. Three dice farkle about 28% of the time, and 200 is well short of the 350 to 400 worth stopping at.

steps.prompt: You have 2,000, your opponent has 3,800, and you have 400 this turn with two dice left. Roll or bank?
steps.explain: Roll. Your opponent needs just 200 and will probably win soon, so banking 400 won’t catch them. Push harder when you’re well behind.
